title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: approving a claim for settlement
content:
## Situation of use

This entry belongs to the Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims product line. It applies when a claim lodged under a cover is approved for settlement, and it fixes the amount written on that approval for every kind of loss except delay loss, which keeps its own delay-loss caps. The approval also records the liability measure that fixed the amount.

## What the tool does

One call of approve_claim_settlement_060ed8c3 books one settlement approval entry on the cover's premium and settlement account for the claim, dated today, marks the claim file as approved, and raises the cover's approved-but-unpaid settlement balance by the approved amount. Nothing is paid out by this call and the cover's status is left unchanged. On success the claimant can be told the approval reference, the amount approved and the recorded liability measure.

## How it is invoked

approve_claim_settlement_060ed8c3 is an internal tool that must first be unlocked (unlock) and then called (call) by the desk agent.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| cover_id | Cover reference number of the cargo liability or CargoCare cover the claim is lodged under, as returned by the cover lookup or the claim file lookup | Identifier |
| claim_id | Claim reference number of the claim file being approved, as returned by the claim file lookup | Identifier |
| booking_id | Booking reference number of the covered shipment the claim concerns, as returned by the booking lookup or shown on the cover | Identifier |
| container_number | Number of the container named in the claim file | ISO 6346, 4 letters followed by 7 digits, written without spaces exactly as the claim file shows it |
| amount_usd | Settlement amount approved for this claim | US dollars, a non-negative number with 2 decimal places; stored rounded half-to-even to 2 decimal places |
| liability_basis | The liability measure that fixed the approved amount | One value from the enum below |

### liability_basis values

- package_limitation: the Hague-Visby per-package limit was the higher limit and capped the loss.
- weight_limitation: the Hague-Visby per-kilogram limit was the higher limit and capped the loss.
- declared_value: the declared value share of the affected packages capped the loss.
- proven_loss: no limit, share, cap or aggregate bound, so the approved amount is the proven loss after any uplift and deductible, including when the invoice value of the affected packages limited the proven loss.
- cover_limit: the product's per-container cover cap bound.
- delay_cap: a delay-loss cap bound.
- aggregate_limit: the annual aggregate still available on the cover reduced the amount.
- not_applicable: never correct for an approval; used only on premium and rejection entries.

## Return

On success the tool returns: status ("approved" when the approval entry was booked); approval_event_id (reference of the new settlement approval entry); claim_id; cover_id; booking_id; container_number (as given); amount_usd (USD with 2 decimal places, as booked); liability_basis (the recorded measure); settlement_payable_usd (the cover's approved-but-unpaid settlement balance after this approval, USD with 2 decimal places).

## Basis Q&A

**Does an approval pay the claimant?** No. The call books the approval and raises the approved-but-unpaid balance; nothing is paid out.

**Does the cover leave the open-claim state on approval?** No. The call leaves the cover's status unchanged.

**Which kind of loss is outside this entry's amount rule?** Delay loss, which keeps its own delay-loss caps.
